task.title: rle-encode
task.statement: The rle package exposes decode (already implemented) and a stub encode(s). Implement encode(s) so that it run-length encodes a string: each maximal run of one character becomes that character followed by the decimal count of the run (the count is always written, even when it is 1). For example encode('aaabbc') is 'a3b2c1', encode('abc') is 'a1b1c1', encode('') is ''. encode must return a str and must round-trip with decode (decode(encode(x)) == x for every string x). Raise TypeError when s is not a string. Do not change decode or the tests.
acceptance_criteria: TypeError when s is not a string

spec.infeasibility_reason: The required encoding format cannot round-trip every string through the unchanged decode. For x='a1', the mandatory encoding is 'a111' (runs 'a1' and '11'), but decode('a111') returns 111 copies of 'a'. The decoder greedily consumes digits as counts, so digit characters cannot always be distinguished from counts. Satisfying the task requires relaxing the universal round-trip requirement or permitting changes to the format and decode.
spec.restated_task: Implement rle.encode(s) to return a string containing each maximal run's character followed by its positive decimal length, including counts of 1; return an empty string for empty input and raise TypeError for non-string inputs. Preserve decode and existing tests. The additional requirement to round-trip every string is incompatible with this format and the existing decoder.

interface_contract.name: rle.encode
interface_contract.behavior: Accept a str, including str subclasses. Process characters as Python string elements, preserving order without normalization. Replace each maximal run with its character followed by the run length in ASCII decimal notation without leading zeros. Always include the count. Return a str; empty input returns ''. The requested universal round-trip guarantee is infeasible.
error_cases: TypeError: s is not an instance of str.

interface_contract.name: rle.decode
interface_contract.behavior: Preserve the existing implementation exactly. Read one character and then greedily consume subsequent characters satisfying isdigit() as its count; convert that count with int(), repeat the character, and concatenate results. Empty input returns ''.
error_cases: TypeError: s is not an instance of str.
ValueError: a parsed character has no following count.
ValueError: int() rejects a consumed count, including some Unicode characters accepted by isdigit().

limitations: Profile 'eval-attest-a1': inference provider codex_gateway; submission runs must use NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory and are labeled separately.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, offers a corrected module. The correction counts only after mechanical validation (same test methods, only the failing tests' bodies changed, passes on the candidate, still fails on the unmodified base or is caught by a mutant, with every result structurally sound and bound to its nonce); the corrected gate is then re-run and the verdict re-derived from the gates. A sealed test that failed by assertion or by an exception, whatever its origin, is never overridden (only a test the supervisor killed at its timeout may be corrected). The classification itself remains a model judgement.

A mutant counts as killed only when a sealed test failed with an authentic child result under a structurally sound supervisor run; lost, forged, incomplete, non-isolated, crashed or timed-out runs are unknown and excluded from the mutation score, and `attest check` recomputes the classification from the raw results.

INFEASIBLE is recorded only when a witness program written by the contract auditor demonstrated the contradiction by running on the unmodified repository (exit code and output recorded); the witness's logic is the model's, its execution is not.
Grounding runs only when the specification names external references; sources are cited, not verified for correctness.
Sandbox CPU/RAM quota controls were not found in the current public REST API; per operation only max_layer_bytes, a timeout and the networking flag are set.
Sandbox raw 'cost' diagnostics are not USD; Codex gateway usage is ChatGPT allowance, not a Nebius charge; Nebius USD is computed from the public price table, not an invoice.
Each run retains one checkpoint image on the service; no image-delete control was found in the current public REST API.

manifest.json lists the sha256 of every artifact and `python -m attest check <run dir or zip>` recomputes digests, the sealed and adversarial bindings from verify_raw.json and the gate-to-verdict rule offline; it cannot re-execute the sandbox runs themselves.

evidence_protocol.note: a VERIFIED bundle of this protocol carries every gate with its raw supervisor result, every evaluated mutant's raw result, the base and mutant evidence of any validated correction, the contract audit and the ledger; an INFEASIBLE bundle carries the executed witness, its digest, output and operation, its analysis in the constrained witness language and copies of the repository files that analysis resolved call origins through; a bundle without this field is historical and is checked for internal consistency only
